weakness.title: Missing Revocation of Lost or Unneeded Access Credentials
weakness.description: Access credentials that are lost, stolen or no longer needed are not revoked, so they remain valid.

extended_description.applicability: Credentials whose holder has left, changed role, ended a contract or lost the credential. Applies to electronic credentials, and to mechanical keys, for which revocation means recovery or re-keying.
extended_description.exploitation: The former holder, or anyone who finds or takes the credential, uses it after it should have stopped working.

row.details: Credentials keep opening entry controls after the right to use them has ended.
Former personnel and finders of lost credentials can reach information, media and equipment.
Entries made with a stale credential appear to belong to a legitimate holder.

row.description: Trigger credential withdrawal from departures, role changes, contract ends and loss reports.
Let holders report a loss at any time, and deactivate the credential immediately.
Compare active credentials with the list of current personnel and contractors, and remove the difference.
Give credentials a limited validity, so that unused ones lapse.
Replace the lock cylinders when a mechanical key is lost or not returned, according to the sensitivity of the area.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-2 Physical Access Authorizations, PS-4 Personnel Termination
